findings.title: findMany method removed (public API break)
findings.body: The previous public method `findMany(findManyArgs)` has been replaced with `getBaseConditions()` returning a raw `Prisma.Sql` fragment. Any external/internal caller that previously invoked `service.findMany({...})` will no longer compile or will silently break at runtime. This is a breaking change but is not mentioned in the PR description, and the migration path (callers must now build their own `$queryRaw` queries and embed `baseConditions` themselves) is not documented. Please confirm no other callers exist in the repo or provide a shim.

findings.title: Caching behaviour tests removed alongside implementation
findings.body: The 'Caching' describe block (previously covering `getAuthorizationConditions` / `getFilterConditions` caching) was deleted in this PR. The service still has `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` fields and still uses the same cache-on-first-call pattern, but there is now zero test coverage for it. A future refactor that breaks caching (e.g. invalidating on filter mutation, key collisions across scopes, or accidental mutation of the cached SQL) will not be caught.

findings.title: getBaseConditions integration test only covers 'user' scope
findings.body: The new `$queryRaw`-based integration test in the 'getBaseConditions' describe block only exercises the `scope: 'user'` path against the real database. The `scope: 'team'` and `scope: 'org'` branches (which are the most complex, with nested AND/OR and `ANY()` arrays) are only compared by stringified SQL and never actually executed against `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized`. Authorization regressions in those branches (e.g. wrong parenthesization, missing `teamId`/`isTeamBooking` clauses, leak across org boundaries) will not be caught by this suite.

findings.title: Dead branches in getBaseConditions
findings.body: `getAuthorizationConditions` is typed `Promise<Prisma.Sql>` and is never null (it always returns either `NOTHING_CONDITION` or a real SQL fragment), so the `else if (authConditions)` branch in `getBaseConditions` is unreachable — `Prisma.Sql` is an object and therefore always truthy. The fallback `else { return NOTHING_CONDITION; }` branch is similarly unreachable. This is harmless dead code but it misleads readers about what can be returned and what combinations are possible.

findings.title: Org scope user list excludes users only on the org membership
findings.body: `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` derives `userIdsFromOrg` from `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds({ teamIds })` where `teamIds` is `[orgId, ...childTeamIds]`. In practice this only returns users who have a membership in the org *or* one of its child teams — but anyone whose membership row points directly at the org but who has no child-team membership is still included, and conversely users who only sit on sub-teams are included. The more subtle problem is the inverse: a user who is *only* an org member via a direct org membership row with no team-level membership is included only because `orgId` is in `teamIds`. If the data ever drifts so the org itself is excluded from `teamIds` (or if the query is later changed to fetch only sub-team memberships to optimize), those users' non-team bookings will silently disappear from org-scope insights. The pre-existing object-based version had the same shape, so this is not a regression, but the SQL rewrite is a good opportunity to make the intent explicit (and to add an integration test for an org member without any sub-team membership).

findings.title: Team scope does not deduplicate userIdsFromTeam
findings.body: `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` deduplicates `userIdsFromOrg` via `Array.from(new Set(userIdsFromOrg))` before binding into `ANY(${uniqueUserIds})`. `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` does the equivalent operation but skips the deduplication step (`const userIdsFromTeam = usersFromTeam.map((u) => u.userId);` is used directly). For a team with many members who happen to share membership rows the resulting `ANY(...)` array can balloon, growing the bound parameter size and the SQL plan unnecessarily. Make the two paths consistent.

findings.title: No afterEach cleanup; failing tests leak database rows
findings.body: Cleanup is implemented as a returned `cleanup()` function that each test must remember to call at the end of its body. If a test fails or throws before reaching the `await testData.cleanup()` line (and there is at least one such path — e.g. the new `$queryRaw` assertion in the `getBaseConditions` describe block, which calls cleanup only after the expect), the user/team/membership/booking/eventType rows it created persist in the shared database, polluting subsequent runs. Wrap `createTestData` in a `try/finally` or use `afterEach(() => testData?.cleanup())` to guarantee cleanup.

findings.title: Integration test does not assert query column shape or count edge cases
findings.body: The only end-to-end `$queryRaw` assertion in the suite (`expect(results).toEqual([{ id: userBooking.id }])`) verifies that *exactly one* row is returned for a user-scoped, single-eventType filter. It does not assert that (a) a booking owned by the same user on a *different* eventType is excluded, (b) a *team* booking for this user is excluded by the `teamId IS NULL` clause, or (c) that the booking row is actually selected from `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` (not just any table that happens to have an `id` column). Adding these assertions is the only way the user-scope SQL is meaningfully exercised.

findings.title: isOrgOwnerOrAdmin replaced .includes with two == comparisons without behavioral justification
findings.body: `isOrgOwnerOrAdmin` was changed from `([MembershipRole.OWNER, MembershipRole.ADMIN] as const).includes(membership.role)` to `(membership.role === MembershipRole.OWNER || membership.role === MembershipRole.ADMIN)`. The two are functionally identical for the enum values in use today, but the new form silently breaks if `MembershipRole` is ever extended with another privileged role — `includes` makes it trivial to add a role to the array, whereas the `||` chain has to be edited in two places. Either keep `.includes` or add a comment explaining the choice.
